summary: Defines a YANG data model for describing Layer 2 network topologies. It extends the generic network and network topology models with attributes specific to Layer 2, so tools can describe and exchange how switches and links are connected.

eli5.summary: This is a standard way for computers to describe a map of which switches and cables are connected at the local-network level.

subtitle: A YANG model for describing which switches, ports and links make up a Layer 2 network.

tldr.problem: The generic YANG network topology model from RFC 8345 has no place for Layer 2 details such as MAC addresses, VLAN tags, link rates or bridge identifiers.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-l2-topology module augments the generic network, node, link and termination point models with Layer 2 attributes, and adds notifications for additions, removals and updates.
tldr.outcome: Nodes and controllers can describe and exchange Layer 2 topologies in a standard form, including physical and virtual ones.

today: RFC 8944 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 8345.

sections.title: Why a Layer 2 Topology Model
sections.content:
RFC 8345 defines YANG models for a generic network and network topology, and says they can be augmented with technology-specific details. RFC 8944 does that for Layer 2 (L2) networks.

The RFC names uses tied to the Interface to the Routing System (I2RS). Nodes can capture their view of the topology and expose it to a network controller. The controller can compare and reconcile its own view with theirs, or even present its view to external applications. The model uses the common types of RFC 6991 and adopts the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342.
sections.eli5: Routers and switches each know their neighbors. This gives them one common way to write that down so a boss computer can check the whole picture.

sections.title: How the Module Fits In
sections.content:
The ietf-l2-topology module is meant to be generic across Layer 2 technologies and can describe both physical and logical (virtual) topologies. It sits on top of ietf-network-topology, which sits on top of ietf-network.

It adds L2-specific identifiers, identities (such as Provider Backbone Bridging, QinQ or VXLAN), attributes and states to networks, nodes, links and termination points. Some of this may be collected through the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) or other Layer 2 protocols, and some may be locally configured.

Learning or configuring advanced technology-specific attributes is out of scope. Dedicated YANG modules should be used instead, for example for TRILL.
sections.eli5: It is a new layer of sticky notes on the existing map. The map stays the same and the notes add local-network details.

sections.title: Attributes of Networks, Nodes, Links and Ports
sections.content:
The module adds a l2-topology presence container to the network types, marking a network as an L2 topology. It then augments four places.

  • Network: a name and a list of flags.
  • Node: name, flags, bridge-id, management-address, management-mac and management-vlan.
  • Link: name, flags, rate (in Kbps), delay (unidirectional, in microseconds), auto-nego (default true) and duplex (full or half).
  • Termination point: interface-name, mac-address, port-number, unnumbered-id, encapsulation-type, VLAN and QinQ tags, lag with member-link-tp, and a vxlan container holding a vni-id.

A termination point is where a link attaches to a node. Flags are identities, so other modules can define new kinds. The encapsulation identities are ethernet, vlan, qinq, pbb, trill, vpls and vxlan.
sections.eli5: Each switch, cable and plug on the map gets a small info card: its name, its address, how fast the cable is, and which VLAN it carries.

sections.title: Features and Notifications
sections.content:
Optional parts are gated by YANG features: VLAN (IEEE 802.1Q tags), QinQ (IEEE 802.1ad double tags) and VXLAN (RFC 7348). The vni type is a 32-bit unsigned value in the range 0 to 16777215, allowing up to 16 M VXLAN segments in one administrative domain; the use of value 0 is implementation specific.

Three notifications report changes: l2-node-event, l2-link-event and l2-termination-point-event. Each carries an event type of addition, removal or update, plus references to the network and element concerned.
sections.eli5: Extras like VLAN tags are optional add-ons. If something on the map changes, the system can send a message saying what was added, removed or changed.

sections.title: The Worked Example
sections.content:
Appendix B gives an instance in JSON encoding with three nodes, D1, D2 and D3, in a network called l2-topo-example. D1 and D2 each have three termination points and D3 has two. There are six links, two between each pair of nodes with one going in each direction.

Termination point 1-0-1 on D1 has lag set to true, with member links 1-0-1-1 and 1-0-1-2. Each point carries a MAC address and each node lists management addresses.
sections.eli5: The example is a tiny map of three switches joined by cables, one of which is really two cables bundled together.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
The data is meant to be accessed with NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040), and access should be restricted with NACM (RFC 8341). A malicious client could add or remove nodes, links or termination points in a configured topology (origin intended), disrupting services. In a learned topology the server prohibits such attempts.

Reading is sensitive too. The topology may expose MAC addresses and VLAN/VXLAN identifiers. Listing MAC addresses allows monitoring of devices and their movements, and location information can be derived from them.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should be allowed to redraw the map or read it, because it shows where devices are.

sections.title: IANA and the Companion Module
sections.content:
IANA registered two XML namespaces and two YANG modules: ietf-l2-topology (prefix l2t) and ietf-l2-topology-state (prefix l2t-s). These are not maintained by IANA.

Appendix A defines ietf-l2-topology-state for implementations that do not support NMDA. It mirrors the main module but augments the state modules ietf-network-state and ietf-network-topology-state, representing operational state.
sections.eli5: There is a second copy of the form for older equipment that stores its current status differently.
